title: What If You Had a Hummingbird's Metabolism?
lines: Gus has to eat a hamburger every three minutes, and that's not even his biggest problem.
It's seven in the morning, and he's just woken up with the metabolism of a hummingbird.
Gram for gram, that tiny bird burns energy fifty times faster than he does.
At his size, that's a hundred and twenty thousand calories a day.
His wife flips pancakes as fast as she can. Gone.
His neighbor laughs that nobody can eat that much, and loses every sausage on the grill.
His heart is beating twenty times a second. That's not a pulse, that's a hum.
But wait. Why is his helmet steaming up?
You see, every calorie he burns turns into heat, and Gus now puts out as much as four space heaters.
Ever notice how a french fry goes cold in minutes, but a baked potato stays hot for half an hour?
Small things have lots of skin for their size. Pound for pound, the hummingbird has about twenty times more than Gus, so its heat just leaks away.
Gus is the baked potato. His temperature climbs more than a degree every minute.
Luckily, he lives by the sea, and cold water carries heat away far faster than air.
Unluckily, his last hamburger was four minutes ago.
And the funny part? Even a hummingbird can't afford to live like a hummingbird.
On cold nights it shuts itself almost completely off, just to make it to breakfast.
